svg.title: Transactional outbox
svg.desc: The transactional outbox of spring-boot-cqrs-jdbc. In one business transaction a command handler saves its changes and calls OutboxEventBus.publish(event), which inserts a row into the cqrs_outbox table (event id, logical name, class name, payload and message context); both commit or both roll back, and publishing without an active transaction throws IllegalStateException. OutboxRelay runs every cqrs.outbox.relay.interval (1 second). Each run is one batch transaction that locks the oldest pending rows, those whose published_at and failed_at are null, with SELECT ... ORDER BY id FETCH FIRST batch-size (100) ROWS ONLY FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so several instances never relay the same row. For each row in order it decodes the row, publishes the event through the target EventBus (KafkaEventBus or RabbitMqEventBus, chosen with cqrs.outbox.relay.event-bus), whose outbound middleware and headers apply, and sets published_at once the bus returned. The batch stops at the first failure. When the target bus fails (broker down, timeout, rejection) the row gets attempts + 1 and last_error and is retried at every later run, forever; it is never set aside. When a row cannot be read (unknown class, payload or context that does not deserialize) it gets read_failures + 1 and the batch stops; once read_failures reaches cqrs.outbox.relay.max-attempts (10) failed_at is set, an ERROR is logged and later rows continue. After the batch transaction commits, OutboxRelayListener beans hear the outcome: OutboxMetrics counts cqrs.outbox.published and cqrs.outbox.publish.failures for this instance, and its gauges cqrs.outbox.pending, cqrs.outbox.set.aside and cqrs.outbox.oldest.pending.age read the whole table. Published rows are deleted after cqrs.outbox.retention (7 days). Delivery is at least once, so consumers should be @Idempotent. The animation inserts row 43, relays row 41, fails on row 42 and stops the batch, then relays rows 42 and 43 in the next run.
svg.text: the row commits with the business change; the relay publishes it after commit, at least once
the batch stops; retried at every run,
unknown class, bad payload or context
several instances can relay: SKIP LOCKED hands every locked batch to one of them
